input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS remediation of KServe and serving data plane images

## Description

This epic removes non-validated cryptographic module usage from the KServe component images and the serving data plane images so that the model serving stack runs correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters with no non-validated crypto in the request path. It produces the module inventory and remediation records that the compliance evidence package is assembled from.

## Scope

- Audit every KServe component image and serving data plane image for linkages to non-validated cryptographic libraries (including transitive dependencies), recording findings as a module inventory (image, library, version, validation status).
- Remediate each finding: rebuild or rebase images so the request path links only validated cryptographic modules.
- Carry required changes in the midstream KServe repositories; upstream contributions only where a change cannot be carried midstream.
- Functionally verify remediated images on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster in both serverless and raw deployment modes (the two supported deployment modes per the architecture context).
- Deliver the module inventory and remediation records for use by the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory covering every KServe component and serving data plane image exists, listing each cryptographic library linkage and its validation status.
- A scan of the remediated images confirms no non-validated cryptographic module is linked in the request path of any serving-stack image.
- Remediated images pass functional verification of the inference request path on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- Each remediated image build is revertible to the prior build (documented rollback path), since this work replaces existing image builds.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path) — this epic delivers that for the KServe components and the serving data plane.

# Platform Operator FIPS compliance

## Description

This epic makes the Platform Operator compliant with the FIPS 140-3 posture of the model serving stack: the operator's own image links only validated cryptographic modules, and the operator correctly deploys and reconciles the serving stack on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters. It produces the operator-side remediation records and test results that feed the compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator image for linkages to non-validated cryptographic libraries (including transitive dependencies).
- Remediate findings so the operator image links only validated cryptographic modules.
- Verify the operator deploys, reconciles, and manages the serving stack (including the FIPS-remediated serving images) on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
- Deliver the operator's module inventory entries, remediation records, and test results for use by the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory entry set covering the Platform Operator image exists, listing each cryptographic library linkage and its validation status.
- A scan of the remediated operator image confirms no non-validated cryptographic module is linked.
- The operator successfully deploys and reconciles the serving stack on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster (CR status reaches Ready for a deployed InferenceService using remediated images).
- The operator image build is revertible to the prior build (documented rollback path), since this work replaces an existing image build.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path) — this epic delivers that for the Platform Operator.

# Compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and steers it through the mandatory security review board milestones to submission at the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventories, remediation records, and FIPS functional test results produced by the serving-stack image remediation (KServe components, serving data plane) and the Platform Operator compliance work.
- Collect build attestations from the serving-stack build pipelines for every image in scope.
- Assemble the evidence package in the format required by the certification process.
- Submit the package through the security review board at the defined milestones, triaging and addressing board feedback.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification laboratory and record its intake status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations, and test results for every serving-stack image in scope (KServe components, serving data plane, and Platform Operator).
- The evidence package is submitted to the security review board at each defined milestone, and board feedback is triaged and addressed.
- The evidence package is submitted to the external accredited certification laboratory, and its intake/triage status is recorded.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification laboratory turnaround is historically six to nine months, and review-board cadence is externally controlled; neither can be compressed by engineering effort. These are schedule risks, not acceptance conditions — the epic's engineering completion point is the assembled, submitted, and triaged package.
- The certification outcome and its timing are outside this strategy's control; the engineering compliance value (FIPS-capable images, CI enforcement, documentation) does not depend on it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab.

# CI gating check for FIPS regressions

## Description

This epic adds a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces non-validated cryptographic module usage, locking in the FIPS-remediated state of the model serving stack.

## Scope

- Implement a build-time check that scans built serving-stack images for non-validated cryptographic library linkage (including transitive dependencies), reusing the detection criteria established by the image remediation audit.
- Wire the check into the serving-stack build pipelines (Konflux), covering all serving-stack builds including the Platform Operator image builds.
- Configure the check as gating: a build fails when non-validated crypto is (re)introduced in the request path.
- Derive the pass/fail baseline from the remediated image set so that only regressions — not the pre-remediation state — fail builds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A build-time check scans serving-stack images for non-validated cryptographic library linkage.
- The check is gating in all serving-stack build pipelines, including the Platform Operator image builds: a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage in the request path fails.
- A verification test injects a known non-validated crypto linkage into a test build and observes the gate fail, confirming the check detects regressions end to end.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS support posture documentation

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, so that customers (notably public-sector) can deploy and operate the compliant stack.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- **FIPS support posture**: what is validated and what is not — the request-path scope of validated cryptographic modules across KServe components, the serving data plane, and the Platform Operator; the certification submission status.
- **Cluster prerequisites**: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, and the deployment modes supported (serverless and raw deployment), including any mode-specific dependencies (for example the service mesh dependency in serverless mode per the architecture context).
- **Operational notes**: how the CI regression gate protects the posture, and what a build failure for non-validated crypto means for consumers of the images.

Out of scope, per the strategy: FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies), and Common Criteria certification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack, including the request-path scope of validated crypto.
- Published documentation lists the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation, including supported deployment modes.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented serving-stack behavior (reviewed by the engineering owners of the remediation and CI work).
- The documentation scope excludes workbenches, pipelines, and training FIPS posture, matching the strategy's out-of-scope statement.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites.
